implication: Entry into CIRP is a material milestone triggering statutory timelines under the IBC: the RP must complete resolution plan evaluation within 180 days (extendable), and all creditors are subject to moratorium — a critical gating event for all stakeholders and creditor recovery strategies.

framework.ref: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (IBC), Ch. II (ss. 4–12)
framework.note: Governs admission, CIRP commencement, RP appointment, and CoC constitution; 'insolvency' defined as inability to pay debts.
Automatic moratorium on all proceedings against debtor; no creditor recovery action possible during CIRP.
RP investigates debtor affairs, prepares Information Memorandum for prospective bidders.
CoC evaluates and votes on resolution plans; 66% threshold for approval.
Plan must be approved within 180 days of CIRP commencement, extendable by 90 days on CoC consent.

framework.ref: SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, Reg. 30
framework.note: Listed companies must disclose CIRP commencement, RP appointment, and material NCLT orders to stock exchanges.
RP must be registered IBBI insolvency professional; governs conduct, fees, and CIRP administration.
NCLT orders appealable to NCLAT within 30 days; further appeal to Supreme Court.

headline: Vikram Solar Limited enters Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process
sum: Vikram Solar Limited, a renewable energy equipment manufacturer, has announced entry into a Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process. The company filed a public announcement on the NSE on 22 June 2026 regarding the commencement of CIRP under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code.
detail: Vikram Solar Limited, a manufacturer and supplier of solar photovoltaic modules and components, initiated the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process following an insolvency petition. The company's disclosure to NSE signals entry into formal resolution proceedings under the IBC, 2016. The exact triggering event (creditor petition vs. management petition), appointment date of the Resolution Professional, and composition of the Committee of Creditors remain to be confirmed from NCLT orders. As a listed entity, the company is bound by additional continuous disclosure obligations under SEBI (LODR) Regulations.
